I can't actually remember how I initially got interested in crossdressing. Part of it in relation, I suppose, to my gender identity - androgynous. I could go off onto a tangent and try to explain it, but the short version is, I'd like to be able to convincingly present as either gender, if I so wish, or androgynously, in the best instance. I always used to enjoy reading gender bender manga - things like Ranma 1/2. I was envious of his ability to change gender with just a bucket of water. I'd kill for that. Not so easy in the real world. Lots of effort has to be put in, to create the right shapes, or the illusions of them, careful shaving, makeup, posture. I can't remember not wanting to be androgynous, that's how far back it goes. Even before I knew the word. But, it's not socially acceptable. So I waited. Eventually, I ended up moving away from home, so here I am. I started crossdressing last year. I can't tell if I'm very good at it too well without anyone else to ask, but I enjoy it. It's nice to wear the clothes I want to wear, and look closer to how I want to look. I think it's important to do the things you enjoy.

For the seventh day of the spring sale there are a few new options, not a lot of games I love though. I'm not going to cover all the games on sale, since they have a ton, but I'll pick some that I feel strongly about from each day.

Shadow Warrior
A first person hack-n-slash with a humorous protagonist. The story is a ludicrous Japanese tale of ninjas and demons, but the main draw is your character's sardonic remarks about the situation. The swordplay is pretty solid as well.

 

Shadow of Mordor
The gameplay in this was solid, with the overall collectables and roaming feeling very much like Assassin's Creed. The combat was pretty easy - somewhat satisfying but would have been better if there was actually a chance of you dieing in a swarm of enemies. Currently you can just dash around and hop over dudes and be nearly invincible unless you mess up. Fun, but not difficult.

My video review is also based on the main game - there have been DLC that may have completed the story, but the main game itself kind of leaves you hanging.

 

Assassin's Creed 4: Black Flag
A lot of the land gameplay is very similar to other Assassin's Creed games, but the sailing in this game is fantastic - and I love all the scenes aboard ships. Those are what really set it apart from similar games and give it a great feel.

 

Doorways 1&2
Linear and not scary, I felt like these were a let down - and didn't really find the story interesting. There is a new chapter out now so maybe that improves the situation.

 

Bridge Constructor
Not my favorite bridge building game, but it's okay. This doesn't have the game elements that Medieval Bridge Constructor does, although it has an unlock system that tries to be a bit more game-like than other titles like Bridge-It.

 

Road Not Taken
I was hoping for a turn-based Binding Of Isaac going into this, but it's very much a puzzle game. The match-three type gameplay feels a bit off because you play an actual character, so it's possible to get yourself trapped. I much prefer Triple Town for not quite as deep, but much more fun gameplay in a similar vein

 

Trine2
I actually prefer this original game to the sequel - it felt a lot more like an adventure through a sandbox, rather than the forced linear nature of some of the sequel puzzles. I wouldn't really call it a puzzle game though - most of it is about platforming while killing enemies.

That said a lot of the pictures sucked (especially at first). But I was wondering if anyone would be willing to look through an album of 20ish images that I thought were the best and help me whittle it down to which ones were my absolute best. I was planning on showing some of these to potential customers/employers as part of my portfolio. The question is are any of them decent enough for that? Or do I still have a long way to go?
